findings.title: Interpolation before $__range check causes incorrect splitting
findings.body: The queries are interpolated with `applyTemplateVariables` before `querySupportsSplitting` is evaluated. `querySupportsSplitting` checks `!isQueryWithRangeVariable(query.expr)`, but after interpolation, `$__range` is replaced with a concrete value, so the check no longer detects it and the query is incorrectly split. This can yield wrong results because the original comment states that such queries must not be split since `$__range` is interpolated on the backend with the split time range.

findings.title: Redundant interpolation of already-interpolated queries
findings.body: In `runShardSplitQuery`, queries are interpolated at lines 49-52 and then passed to `splitQueriesByStreamShard`. Inside that function, for each shard group, `runSplitQuery` is called (line 163) which will again interpolate the targets (querySplitting.ts line 299). This double interpolation is redundant and may cause performance overhead, especially with many shards, and could lead to unexpected behavior if interpolation is not idempotent or has side effects.

findings.title: Possible mutation of request targets if applyTemplateVariables mutates in place
findings.body: The `.map((query) => datasource.applyTemplateVariables(query, ...))` passes the original query objects. If `applyTemplateVariables` mutates the query (as the mocks in tests do), the original `request.targets` are mutated, which can affect other consumers of the request object, including tracking (`trackGroupedQueries`) or subsequent calls. The implementation should ensure a new object is returned, or the mapping should clone the query before interpolation.
